45.author: St. John Chrysostom
45.work: Homilies on the Gospel of St. Matthew, Homily 47
45.text: Chrysostom asks why Christ compares the Kingdom to a merchant seeking pearls. The merchant in the parable is not a man stumbling on treasure by chance, as the previous parable described; he is one who has been looking, who knows the trade, who has seen many beautiful things and can tell the unrivaled from the merely fine. The point is that for some the Gospel is found because they sought it. They asked. They tried other answers. When they saw Christ they recognized at once what they had been looking for, and gave up everything to obtain Him.

45.author: St. Gregory the Theologian
45.text: Gregory the Theologian uses the pearl image for Holy Baptism itself. Baptism, he says, is the one purchase the Christian makes that costs him everything he has and gives him a kingdom in return. The merchant of the parable is the catechumen who has counted the cost; the field is the world he sells; the pearl is the new life into which the waters of Baptism deliver him.
